Transcript: scripts/diag_threads.py  (2026-09-15, containerised)
Purpose: find out why small PyTorch ops appeared implausibly slow in run env-bench-01.
Machine state: CONTENDED (37 unrelated containers running; see GAPS G-008). Treat all timings
               as lower bounds.

==============================================================================
CPU / CGROUP FACTS
==============================================================================
  os.cpu_count                     12
  len(os.sched_getaffinity)        12
  torch.get_num_threads            6
  torch.get_num_interop_threads    12
  OMP_NUM_THREADS                  6
  cgroup_v2_cpu.max                max 100000      <-- no Docker CPU quota
  cgroup_v1_quota_us               unavailable (FileNotFoundError)
  cgroup_v1_period_us              unavailable (FileNotFoundError)
  nproc                            6

  128          0.104       0.076       0.092       0.099

==============================================================================
  threads=1     120.55 ms/step        8494 tok/s   (inner=5)
  threads=2     100.45 ms/step       10194 tok/s   (inner=12)

==============================================================================
VERDICT
==============================================================================
  128x128 matmul: 1 thread     103.5 us   6 threads      98.7 us   ratio   0.95x
  -> H2 CONFIRMED: the earlier floor was a measurement artefact; amortised timing fixes it.
  fastest training step at threads=2: 100.4 ms
  written to evidence/env/thread_diagnosis.json

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT THIS ESTABLISHED
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. env-bench-01's numbers were produced by a faulty harness, not by slow hardware. Timing a
   single call per sample carried a large fixed entry cost (consistent with PyTorch's intra-op
   thread pool parking between calls and being rewoken under a hypervisor). Amortising many
   calls inside one timed region removed it:
       128x128 matmul   31.68 ms  ->   0.104 ms   (~300x)
       2048x2048        252.2 ms  ->  95.76 ms    (68 -> 179 GFLOP/s)
       0.53M step       4979.7 ms -> 100.45 ms    (~50x)
2. Docker imposes no CPU quota (`cpu.max = max 100000`), so the container is not being throttled.
3. Thread count is workload-dependent, and this held in every run:
       small ops / small models  -> 2 threads is best; 6 threads is actively harmful
       large matmuls             -> scales to 6 threads (179 GFLOP/s at 2048^2)
   Project 1's training loop therefore pins 2 threads, not 6.
